# Isleta 2.3.0
The volume and brightness bars in the notch are controls now: press or drag one and the level goes there. Press anywhere else on them and they get out of the way.
## New
- **Drag the volume or brightness bar in the notch.** Press anywhere along it to send the level there, or hold and drag to slide it. The bar is a few points tall and what you can aim at is much taller, so you do not have to be precise about it. - **Press the middle of the notch to put a level away and open the island.** The reading goes, and the island opens on whatever you were last looking at — the player, if something is playing.
## Improved
- **A video in a browser shows the browser's icon instead of a music note.** Anything playing without cover art — a Safari tab, a video on a site that publishes none — now says which app the sound is coming from, on every surface that draws a cover. - **The island no longer springs at the end of a range until you ask twice.** Running the volume or brightness all the way down leaves the island where it is; the *next* press on the key is what makes it lean, and it keeps leaning for as long as you hold it.
## Fixed
- **Nothing appears on screen while the Mac is still unlocking.** Plugging in the charger — or anything else the island announces — part way through the unlock used to draw the island over the top of it. It waits in the notch now, and arrives once the unlock has finished. - **A film's remaining time is no longer cut off.** Anything over an hour showed `-1:0…` where the countdown belonged; the two times either side of the scrub bar now make room for the hours, and give the room back on tracks that do not need it.
## Requirements
macOS 26 or later, on Apple Silicon. Displays with a real notch get the island; a Mac without one gets a floating island on the main display.
## Known limitations
- **The lean at the end of a range needs Accessibility.** Reaching the end of the volume or brightness no longer moves the island on its own, and the press after it is only visible to Isleta with that permission granted. The reading itself, and the bar filling and emptying, work either way. - **A muted Mac's bar cannot be dragged.** It is drawn at nothing whatever the volume behind it is, so pressing it opens the island instead. Unmute first. - **You cannot see who is calling.** macOS does not let apps outside Apple read that, or answer for you. Isleta shows that a call is happening and nothing more. - **Weather needs your location, or a city you type.** Isleta asks for neither until you use it. - **A connected device's battery is read once, when it connects.** It does not tick down as you wear them, and most non-Apple headphones report no level at all. - **A timer started by Siri, Shortcuts or Control Center can take a few seconds to appear.** One started by hand in Clock is there immediately. - **Replacing the system HUDs is on by default, and it needs Accessibility.** Two switches in Settings hand the keys back. Quitting Isleta hands them back too; if Isleta is force-quit, the system HUD stays out of the way until Isleta next starts. Brightness covers the built-in display only. - **Apple's own banner still appears when headphones connect.** It is drawn by the menu bar rather than by the HUD helper Isleta can stand in for, so the island announces the connection alongside it rather than instead of it. - **The island sits above Mission Control.** In a real notch it covers nothing; a floating island can sit over the middle of the space labels. - **Today and tomorrow show five entries and then a count.** A busy pair of days says how many it could not fit rather than scrolling.

# Isleta 2.2.0
The music page is there when there is music. On a quiet Mac the island turns between two pages instead of three, and the sound the Mac makes when you unlock it is now a switch of its own.
## New
- **A switch for the unlock sound.** Settings ▸ General ▸ Lock Screen has its own control for the short sound Isleta plays when you come back and the Mac unlocks. It is set to whatever your Mac was already doing, so nothing changes until you change it.
## Improved
- **The island stops showing a player with nothing in it.** With nothing playing, a two-finger swipe goes from the day straight to the weather and the dots under the notch say two. Start something and the page is back between them; the small player beside your day is unchanged. - **A track ending never turns the page under you.** If you are looking at the player when the music stops, it stays put and says "Not playing" until you swipe away or close the island. - **"Welcome back" no longer arrives with page dots under it.** The greeting opens the island by itself, so the row of dots is left off. It is back the next time you open the island yourself. - **The island still remembers the player.** If that is where you live, closing the island on a quiet Mac brings you back to the day — and the next time something is playing, back to the player.
## Requirements
macOS 26 or later, on Apple Silicon. Displays with a real notch get the island; a Mac without one gets a floating island on the main display.
## Known limitations
- **You cannot see who is calling.** macOS does not let apps outside Apple read that, or answer for you. Isleta shows that a call is happening and nothing more. - **Weather needs your location, or a city you type.** Isleta asks for neither until you use it. - **A connected device's battery is read once, when it connects.** It does not tick down as you wear them, and most non-Apple headphones report no level at all. - **A timer started by Siri, Shortcuts or Control Center can take a few seconds to appear.** One started by hand in Clock is there immediately. - **Replacing the system HUDs is on by default, and it needs Accessibility.** Two switches in Settings hand the keys back. Quitting Isleta hands them back too; if Isleta is force-quit, the system HUD stays out of the way until Isleta next starts. Brightness covers the built-in display only. - **Apple's own banner still appears when headphones connect.** It is drawn by the menu bar rather than by the HUD helper Isleta can stand in for, so the island announces the connection alongside it rather than instead of it. - **The island sits above Mission Control.** In a real notch it covers nothing; a floating island can sit over the middle of the space labels. - **Today and tomorrow show five entries and then a count.** A busy pair of days says how many it could not fit rather than scrolling.

# Isleta 2.1.2
The player names your audio again — "Lossless", "Hi-Res Lossless", "Dolby Atmos" — which 2.1.1 could lose for the rest of a session.
## Fixed
- **The audio format no longer disappears when you stop the music.** In 2.1.1 the line under the artist went away the first time playback stopped, and resuming the same playlist did not bring it back — only a new track or restarting Isleta did. It stays with the track it describes now. - **And it comes back when you quit your player and open it again.** Isleta now asks for the format when a track is playing without one, rather than waiting for a queue change — so it no longer takes a press of next and then previous to see "Lossless" again. This one was never right, in any version.
